at åbne.explanation: "At åbne" means "to open". You can open a door, a shop or a bank account. "Hvornår åbner I?" (When do you open?) is what you ask a shop or office. It is the opposite of "at lukke" (to close). On signs you will see "Åben" (open) and "Lukket" (closed).

sentence.en: The shop opens at nine o'clock.

et år.explanation: "Et år" means "a year". It is also how you give your age: "Jeg er tredive år gammel" means "I am thirty years old". "I år" means "this year" and "næste år" means "next year".

åben.explanation: "Åben" means "open", for doors, shops and windows, and also for people who are open-minded. The opposite is "lukket" (closed). The similar-looking "at åbne" means "to open" (an action), while "åben" describes how something is: "Butikken er åben" (The shop is open).

sentence.en: The shop is open until six o'clock.

åbningstider.explanation: "Åbningstider" means "opening hours", the times when a shop or an office is open. It is always used in the plural: "Hvad er jeres åbningstider?" (What are your opening hours?). It is made of "åbning" (opening) and "tider" (times).

sentence.en: What are the opening hours today?
